title: I used generative AI on Thistlelight, a five-garden browser platformer
author: Brunsous_Monitor6037
selftext:
Hi r/aigamedev — I’m sharing Thistlelight, my small commercial browser platformer, and a bit about the AI-assisted workflow. I used generative AI assistance for code, graphics, and text; those categories are disclosed on the itch.io page.

The game follows a lantern moth through five moonlit gardens. Each has three lost seeds to collect, then a glowing archway to reach with jump, glide, and a light dash. It runs as a Canvas game in the browser, with English and Italian text, keyboard and touchscreen controls, checkpoints, and local progress saving.

Keeping it to one small, self-contained browser project made it possible to iterate on the movement, scenes, and bilingual copy together. It’s sold on itch.io for a minimum of €1: https://brunosudhuwb.itch.io/thistlelight

I’m happy to discuss what AI assisted and what the build process looked like.
